findings: src/sim.js drive resolves tank contact after walls, so placing the player at (-10.2, 8), heading 90, and computer at (-11.4, 10.2), then holding W for five steps pushes the player inside the inner wall.
src/ai.js discards waypoints within 0.5 units before reaching a clear firing line, leaving the computer permanently stationary without firing when the player is at (0, 12).
src/sim.js stepShells checks only step endpoints, so a shell fired from (-5, 0), heading 0, passes through the computer's collision circle at (0, 1.449) without causing damage.
src/sim.js misses tangent tank hits: firing from (-5,0) at heading 0 past a tank at (0,1.45) leaves its health at 100 despite shell contact.
src/sim.js checks wall contact only at shell endpoints, allowing a shell from (-9.1,4.76) at heading 315 to cross the wall corner at (-9,5) without bouncing.
src/tools.js accepts place without heading instead of rejecting missing input, adding an untested optional-heading behavior.
The site lacks /llms.txt describing its WebMCP tools, as required by the supplied repository instructions.
src/geom.js pushOut ignores exact wall contact: firing from (-14, 4.75) heading 0 passes tangentially along the inner wall with bounces remaining 0.
src/tools.js coerces invalid inputs to {}, so reset([]) resets the game and returns ok:true instead of the required error.
src/tools.js rounds each step duration independently, so 100 calls requesting 0.01 seconds with W held move the tank 10 units instead of the required 6 units over one second.
